card.name: Adverbs ending in -ly before a verb or adjective
card.fires_on: Whole adverbs ending in -ly (Originally, Currently, solely, typically, potentially, fully, apparently, Clearly) that sit before a participle, adjective or clause. The pole is most active when the adverb opens a phrase.

modes.label: Sentence-opening adverbs
modes.description: An adverb like Originally, Currently or Clearly starts a note or sentence, such as source credits or status lines.
modes.example: Chefs Talk The Science Of Savory <<Originally>> published on Tue October 16,

modes.label: Adverbs before adjectives or participles
modes.description: An adverb sits mid-sentence and modifies the next adjective or verb form.
modes.example: used with other<< potentially>> nephrotoxic drugs.

card.writes: It suppresses the -ly ending, so it discourages adding another adverb ending after an adverb that is already complete.
card.plain: It fires on a finished adverb such as 'currently' or 'originally' and signals that the next word is not another -ly ending.
